text:
anya: FYI we're about to start a bulk opt-in for v2 on Monday. Before we do, we need a clear console "compatibility mode" indicator and telemetry to show any transient extra costs during the first 10 minutes after a tenant flips.

liam: +1. Can we define "transient" precisely? Is it warmup only (KV/cache misses) or also model variant fallbacks that increase tokens?

priya: Both. Observed patterns: initial prefix miss + repeated short sessions causing regen -> higher tokens. Suggest we expose two numbers: `warmup_tokens_est` and `fallback_tokens_est`. Keep them distinguishable in telemetry.

eng-bot: note: previous rollout for 2025-10-03 showed median warmup minutes = 3, 95th pct = 7.

anya: Good data. UX asks: the console pill should say "compat mode: v2 (migrating)" with a small "monitor" link. Clicking goes to a panel with estimated $ impact and a toggle to pause auto-migrate.

sam: Telemetry plan: add event tags `version_handshake`, `migration_phase` (values: prewarm, fallback, steady), and a sampled `billing_estimate` field. We should sample body-level tags at 1% but always emit aggregated per-tenant counters every 1m.

liam: Concern: sampling will miss short spikes. Proposal: when a tenant flip is detected, temporarily raise sampling to 10% for that tenant for 10 minutes (ephemeral). That gives better granularity without increasing overall cardinality much.

priya: Agree. Also add a derived metric `tenant.migration_cost_delta.1m` that is (tokens_in_migration_phase - baseline_tokens_1m_prior). This gives a delta for quick alerting.

eng-bot: alert rule suggestion: trigger if `migration_cost_delta.1m` > 50% and > 500 tokens for a tenant for 2 consecutive minutes.

product-ux: For copy, avoid scary words: use "temporary increase expected during migration" and show recommended actions: pause auto-migrate, roll back, or contact SE. Also include a one-click export of data for billing disputes.

anya: Ops suggestion: implement a soft-shadow mode for large accounts: route 5% of traffic to v2 but bill as v1 for first 5 minutes; show estimated costs side-by-side. Helps customers opt-in without risk.

liam: Can the router emit `route_origin=console` vs `route_origin=autoswitch`? Product wants to know if auto decisions are causing spikes.

sam: Yes, add `route_origin` tag. We'll also emit `migration_start_ts` so queries can align windows. Example query for the panel:

```
SELECT tenant_id,
  sum(case when migration_phase='prewarm' then tokens else 0 end) as warmup_tokens,
  sum(case when migration_phase='fallback' then tokens else 0 end) as fallback_tokens,
  sum(tokens) as total_tokens
FROM request_events
WHERE migration_start_ts >= now() - interval '20 minutes'
GROUP BY tenant_id
ORDER BY total_tokens DESC
LIMIT 100;
```

priya: Nice. Also capture `seq_len_distribution` during migration vs baseline; some customers have lots of short seq requests that amplify the change.

product-ux: Console mock: top-line banner "Migration in progress" with small pill showing minutes left (auto-calc from migration_start_ts + window). Panel sections: summary (est $), timeline chart, breakdown (warmup/fallback/steady), actions (pause/revert/notify).

liam: One more policy ask: during migration we should temporarily freeze quota throttles until warmup finishes, to avoid client retries causing extra tokens. But that could allow runaway usage. Maybe instead apply token-saver mode: reduce max seq-len for the first 3 minutes unless tenant overrides.

anya: I prefer token-saver mode. We'll default to conservative seq-len cap and surface a "permit longer sequences" button in the panel (with clear billing note).

sam: Implementation checklist: 1) router flags for route_origin & migration_start_ts (liam), 2) telemetry tags + sampling bump logic (sam), 3) aggregated migration metrics & alert rule (priya), 4) console pill + panel + actions (product-ux), 5) soft-shadow billing mode for canaries (anya).

priya: I'll draft the aggregator and exporter endpoints. Can we run a canary on 50 tenants next week?

anya: Yes, schedule will be posted in the migration runbook. I'll own canary coordination and support playbook.

liam: I'll land the router changes and add an opt-out header `X-Compat-Mode: prefer-v1` to let clients opt out of auto-migration per-request.

product-ux: I'll share mocks and the email template for proactively notifying customers when their estimated delta exceeds thresholds.

eng-bot: link: migration runbook doc -> docs/internal/migrations/v2-compatibility.md

anya: Thanks team. Please add any blockers here. If nobody objects, we'll start instrumenting tomorrow. :rocket:
